title: Council Post: Navigating Tomorrow: Unraveling The Impact Of AI On Today's Workforce
text:
Career coach and LinkedIn expert (Linked Into Jobs); author and founder of The Job Search School. Learn how to find your dream job.
As we all know, ever-advancing artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the landscape of today’s workforce. And this is a big concern to most people. But I think those worries come primarily from not understanding what is happening now and what is coming in the world of AI. As AI evolves, it is imperative to understand its use and implications and proactively prepare for the changes AI can bring. So let’s unpack what the advancement of AI means in the workforce.
Think Augmented Intelligence, Not Replacement Intelligence
One of the common misconceptions is that AI was created to replace humans. Contrary to the fears of widespread job loss, AI is better viewed as "assisted" or "augmented" intelligence. Instead of entirely replacing human roles, AI is meant to assist and enhance human capabilities.
A good example of this is customer service. We have seen where AI has significantly transformed customer service, streamlining processes and enhancing customer experiences. AI-driven chatbots and virtual assistants handle routine queries, providing quick and accurate responses 24/7. AI can provide quick responses to routine tasks, but it does little to calm an upset customer as it does not have the human touch. Humans are still needed for more complex problem-solving tasks, and they are also needed to build relationships with clients or potential customers.
AI can automate certain tasks, but it does not necessarily eliminate jobs—though it does transform them. I believe that customer service jobs now will be more focused on tasks that require emotional intelligence, creativity, critical thinking and ethical considerations. Human customer service agents will become more like relationship managers, and the AI will take care of the routine tasks.
Skill Evolution In The AI Era
Now that we have discovered that jobs will not be replaced, but rather transformed, let's look at how the rise of AI will lead to the need for a skills evolution in today’s workplace. The emphasis will shift to human skills such as creativity, problem-solving, emotional intelligence and critical thinking.
Here are a few examples of this skill shift:
Financial Services
Transaction processing, routine customer inquiries and basic financial analysis can be automated and taken over by AI. So people in those jobs need to upskill to be able to handle roles that include complex financial advisory, relationship building and fraud detection, all of which require human cognitive abilities.
Education
Automated grading, routine lesson planning and basic tutoring tasks can be taken over by AI. Teachers with AI-assisted classrooms would need to switch their skills to inspirational teaching, mentoring and understanding diverse student needs, along with teaching strategies that work for groups and others for individual instruction.
Software Development
Automated code testing, debugging and basic algorithmic tasks can be taken over by AI. So software development roles will need to upskill or cross-skill to include creative problem-solving, user experience design and strategic software architecture.
Adapting To The New Workplace
The workplace is becoming a collaborative arena where humans and AI work side by side. AI algorithms process vast datasets at incredible speeds, providing insights that empower human decision-making. The synergy between human intuition and AI precision is the future of efficiency.
As the job landscape evolves, driven by the transformative power of AI, opportunities are boundless—they aren’t going away. Rather, companies are reshaping their operations, and workers need to adapt.
Here's your guide to not only surviving but thriving in this era of AI-induced changes:
1. Think outside the box. Employers are actively seeking candidates who can adapt to new technologies. Your ability to embrace change can set you apart.
2. Continuous learning is key. In a world where technology is evolving rapidly, the concept of a static skill set is outdated. Continuous learning is not just a buzzword; it's a survival strategy. Consider online courses, certifications and workshops to stay updated with the latest trends in your industry.
3. Upskilling opens new avenues. Upskilling is your ticket to new opportunities in the workforce. Research and identify the skills that complement your current expertise and are in demand in the AI era. Whether it's data analysis, programming or project management, upskilling enhances your value.
4. A growth mindset is a game changer. Embrace challenges as opportunities to grow. Understand that your abilities can be developed with dedication and hard work. AI may change the game, but your growth mindset ensures you stay in it and aren’t left behind.
Final Thoughts
By upskilling, fostering adaptability and embracing a collaborative mindset, individuals can navigate the AI-driven future successfully. In essence, the teamwork between humans and AI is creating a harmonious collaboration where each contributes its unique strengths. AI's proficiency in data analysis, pattern recognition and automation complements the creativity, emotional intelligence and nuanced decision-making abilities of humans. This collaborative partnership is not about replacement but about augmenting human capabilities, leading to a more dynamic and innovative workforce.
As John F. Kennedy once said, "Change is the law of life. And those who look only to the past or the present are certain to miss the future."
The AI-driven future is not a distant vision—it's here. By understanding its dynamics and preparing today, the workforce can turn the challenges of AI into stepping stones for a more prosperous and innovative tomorrow.

title: Council Post: How AI Is Adding Faster Funding And Efficiency To Small-Business Lending
text:
Richard Gusmano is the Founder and CEO of Business Credit Consultants, a digital financial consulting practice for small business owners.
In the not-so-distant past, applying for a small-business loan was a cumbersome process involving multiple trips to the bank, heaps of financial records and face-to-face meetings with loan officers. The credit acquisition landscape was intentionally opaque, with banks holding all the power. However, the advent of the online business environment has ushered in a new era, reducing the need for physical visits to banks. Yet challenges persist in the form of time-consuming processes, extensive documentation requirements and hidden barriers to loan approvals.
The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) is revolutionizing the small-business lending landscape, offering solutions to the long-standing hurdles. AI’s advances empower small-business owners, providing them with insights to make informed choices, submit stronger credit applications and secure loan approvals more expeditiously. The transformative impact of AI extends beyond mere automation; it empowers businesses to take control of their financial health by bringing transparency to lending decisions.
With a decade of experience guiding entrepreneurs through the small-business lending process, the recognition of AI’s value in streamlining application preparation is evident to me. At my company, where approximately 7,000 files from small-business owners are processed annually, an AI-driven digital loan qualifying system plays a pivotal role. This system efficiently collects crucial data points, offering visibility pre-application and enabling owners to make informed adjustments.
Here are key areas where AI is reshaping the small-business lending landscape:
Borrowers Gain Faster Funding And Data With Value
AI’s ability to streamline complex processes that have historically caused delays can reduce loan funding from weeks to days, eliminating the threat of cash flow problems.
AI can now serve as a loan-qualifying system to analyze credit reports and a business owner’s creditworthiness as viewed by lenders. This AI analysis and industry expertise can translate intricate financial information into actionable insights for owners before they apply for a loan. Accurate AI data that analyzes a business’s financials gives small-business owners their lending eligibility within minutes and potential avenues for finance.
These insights allow borrowers to understand potential stumbling blocks and rectify issues before applying for credit, significantly reducing the waiting time associated with credit decisions. While AI data provides the road map to securing a line of credit, small-business owners can also turn to trusted consultants for recommendations on the right steps to ensure adjustments are completed before applying. Real-time insight into the data that banks utilize when making expedited or streamlined business lending decisions is time and money for business owners.
When business owners use AI data to make lending decisions at the start of their loan application, they may be able to better avoid denials, which can delay a business from obtaining funding for months.
Personalized Customer Experiences For Borrowers
AI’s ability to process vast amounts of data allows lenders to offer custom services to business owners. Knowing what lenders will need to qualify, AI has the capability to secure the essential information to generate the necessary data points, such as personal credit, business-to-business credit, NAICS code or entity type, available credit, time in business, inquiries, Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) filings and tax liens, if needed. AI algorithms can generate tailored financial recommendations by analyzing transaction histories, market trends and individual financial behaviors.
This customizable approach goes beyond conventional lending practices, allowing businesses to access funding options that align precisely with their unique needs. For instance, an AI-powered lending platform might recommend a specific loan with terms and conditions tailored to a particular small business’s financial health, goals and business type.
Improved Consistency And Speed In Underwriting For Lenders
AI is helping creditors leverage their lending talent, aggregating and automating the knowledge and expertise of seasoned underwriters.
This helps minimize the risk of encountering underwriters unfamiliar with a business owner’s financial intricacies. It also reduces the chance of errors when accompanied by regular audits by seasoned professionals who know what is required for borrowers in various spaces.
AI is there to augment, collect and automate the various data points and filing that can be done digitally with speed. A human touch is required to interpret all variables and provide next steps to achieve the desired outcome of a line of credit. Experienced underwriting professionals can shift their focus to oversight and regulation audits to ensure each borrower benefits from a comprehensive evaluation.
Document Preparation And Collection For Lenders
Through ML algorithms, AI optimizes processes and workflows, making them more responsive to the changing demands of businesses. AI systems, such as the one that powers my own company, are customized to gather and house the documentation needed for various applications.
This speeds up document collection and gives lenders valuable AI credit insight into applications. Adaptability helps ensure lending institutions can keep pace with emerging trends without expensive upgrades to their current technology.
Continuous Improvement And Innovation For All
As AI algorithms become more refined, lenders can leverage them to adapt to market trends and economic shifts, providing accurate credit standings for borrowers. AI fosters innovation in the design, security and delivery of financial services, leading small-business owners to smarter lending solutions.
However, it’s crucial to note that the use of AI in lending requires ongoing refinement and guidelines. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau issued guidance in September 2023 on credit denials from lenders using AI, emphasizing the need for human oversight and governance. Entrepreneurs should not rely solely on AI when making credit decisions.
While AI is transforming bank lending, risks remain, and mistakes must be addressed. The industry is on the brink of a transformative journey where forward-thinking banks and lenders embrace AI-powered solutions, attracting qualified, organized and ready-to-apply small businesses. The ongoing evolution of AI, with the right support and values, promises to reshape banking and small-business lending, unlocking new possibilities beyond legacy systems.

title: Council Post: Operational Data Lakes: Why They're Needed In Your 2024 AI Strategy
text:
Ranjan is the Chief Product and Technology Officer at Apica.
For IT teams, cutting tech debt and reducing toil is most likely at the top of their 2024 New Year’s resolutions. In the ever-evolving landscape of data management and artificial intelligence (AI), businesses are increasingly turning to operational data lakes to do just that: store and harness operational data as efficiently as possible.
Operational data lakes can play an important role in fueling AI strategies and have a lot of potential for driving business success. The key is understanding what they are and how to best incorporate them into your AI strategy.
Understanding Operational Data Lakes
In any enterprise, data comes from multiple types of software. One of these types of data is business intelligence (BI), consisting of analytical, marketing and inventory data. Another type of data is operational, which is used to understand the performance, reliability or availability of certain things in the enterprise's software, making it crucial for IT, security and cybersecurity domains. Operational data lakes serve as centralized repositories for operational data, facilitating the storage and analysis of information derived from various sources such as software, cloud environments and machine-generated data.
Why Operational Data Lakes Matter
Operational data, often ephemeral and transient, requires a dedicated solution to capture and store these short-lived data points. For example, if you're monitoring a machine that tracks temperature control or looking at a system and monitoring CPU utilization, the values don’t stay constant for very long—they'll fluctuate. You end up with multiple point-in-time snapshots and need somewhere to house them all. The data lake becomes the reservoir for these fleeting insights, offering historical context and enabling organizations to make informed decisions based on past trends and performance metrics. With a centralized location for operational data, you can ask questions like, "Does this machine always run hot?" or "Does this server always run slow?"
The Importance Of Contextualized Data For AI
The thing about AI is that it's only as effective as the data it relies on. You can make conclusions based on contextualized data if you have it, but without it, you'll draw incorrect conclusions. Let’s pretend we're working with a generative AI system and we say, "A dog has four legs, a dog is an animal, a cat has four legs, a cat is an animal, a table has four legs. What is a table?" Without context, the generative AI system will say, "A table is an animal" because that's the only context it has. Now, if you add more context to this data, such as, "A table is a piece of furniture," then when you ask the question, the AI will provide the right answer.
We need to start thinking about AI and its ability to predict things similarly to how we view the inner workings of the human brain. The more data you supply, the better the context will be, leading to more precise analytics, forecasts and deductions. The key to any AI system is massive amounts of contextualized data.
Gartner analysts recently shared that ChatGPT alone uses the same amount of energy as 33,000 households each day. That's a massive amount of energy required for this generative AI tool to function. Just as these tools require massive amounts of energy, they also require massive amounts of data to make better business decisions and ensure your infrastructure is performing.
Operational data lakes house all of this data. They play a pivotal role in AI by providing a holistic view of the enterprise, ensuring that AI models have access to these massive amounts of contextualized data. This contextual richness is essential for accurate predictions, analytics and intelligent inferences, echoing the sentiment that more data—particularly contextual data—leads to more accurate AI outcomes.
Putting Operational Data Lakes To Use
One of the simplest yet most effective ways generative AI can be used within systems is by adding context to cryptic operational data. We can use generative AI to look at databases that have already been indexed and ask questions to gain an understanding. From translating acronyms to providing real-time explanations of keywords, generative AI simplifies complex data, making it more accessible and actionable.
Operational data lakes can assist AI in identifying anomalous patterns as well. For example, let’s say an enterprise typically has 100 users logging into its systems on a daily basis, but one morning, traffic patterns report 500 people logging in. This would be an anomaly and a potential security threat that AI systems could detect, assuming it's been provided and trained with contextualized amounts of data stored in operational data lakes.
Enhancing Efficiency In 2024 And Beyond
Innovation is rapidly evolving, and to survive, businesses must embrace these changes. The alternative could lead to increased latency in decision-making, hindering a company's ability to innovate and thrive in a rapidly changing business landscape. Understanding operational data lakes and viewing them as an important component of an AI strategy is imperative.
Prioritize and strengthen your AI strategies in 2024 by selecting solutions that offer adaptability, performance and the ability to seamlessly integrate with anything, anywhere. You want a solution that simplifies data storage, offers an open data format and allows for complete data storage ownership. These characteristics can lead to data storage solutions that are not only convenient but also profitable. Work with a solution that will work for you.
By centralizing data and normalizing structures, operational data lakes help eliminate fragmented data silos, reducing ad hoc automation and streamlining processes. The net result is a significant decrease in toil and tech debt, freeing up resources for more strategic initiatives. Make 2024 the year you harness the power of operational data lakes to help propel your AI initiatives to success.

title: Council Post: Seven Keys To Making Generative AI Work For Your Business
text:
Executive Director, Institute for Experiential AI at Northeastern University, Founder and Chairman, Open Insights.
On Oct. 18, 2023, I attended and participated in the Leading With AI Responsibly conference hosted by my institution, the Institute for Experiential AI. I came out with many insights from this meeting, in which business leaders shared several in-depth stories about how they’re using generative AI (GenAI) to drive business success today.
The discussions reinforced my long-held belief that a successful AI strategy requires a few specific principles for businesses that want to gain a competitive advantage with AI while avoiding its many pitfalls. Below I share seven keys for making generative AI work for businesses.
1. Human oversight brings success.
The effective use of AI, especially in business, hinges on human involvement. If humans aren’t providing oversight and feedback, models can quickly go off the rails for even the most seemingly simple applications. "Experiential AI" is the term we use for AI with a human in the loop, and we see confirmation of this in every working AI deployment out there.
An example is using large language models (LLMs) to expedite the creation of FAQ content on your website while using human reviewers to ensure the content is accurate and of high quality before publishing. Such an approach allows you to leverage the speed and productivity gains of AI while avoiding the pitfalls of using AI irresponsibly. This is especially important in highly regulated industries like finance and health care, but the risks of using AI irresponsibly extend to almost every industry. Responsible AI solutions that work with and learn from human intelligence are a better path to building working solutions that avoid the pitfalls of autonomous AI.
2. Create a sandbox.
Executives also need a thoughtful and controlled approach to implementing generative AI. A crucial tenet of this strategy is the creation of a "sandbox" environment, akin to a laboratory, where developers can experiment with and refine AI applications. This approach ensures that AI development is done responsibly and safely with a strong emphasis on data protection and ethical considerations.
For instance, companies could create internal software environments that offer developers a controlled space to experiment with AI applications. This approach encourages innovation without creating new risks. Many companies target the output of these AI models for use by their employees to evaluate fit and correctness and do not allow such applications to deal with external parties directly, thus limiting risks while learning from the sandboxed efforts.
3. Keep applications narrow.
One unfortunate byproduct of the endless AI hype is that some people believe they can build one AI model that does everything for their business. That approach simply doesn’t work and leads to unnecessary waste of resources and time. AI applications should instead be focused and narrow.
It’s important to clearly define AI use cases early on in model development. This approach minimizes potential risks and guides decisions on model techniques, data requirements, and legal or ethical issues. The lesson here is to keep your applications as narrow and as precisely defined as possible—general AI is the enemy of today’s successful deployments!
4. Data and context are key.
We all know that most working AI is highly dependent on learning algorithms (which include generative AI algorithms), and it is obvious that ML and data science require data. The data captured has to be fine-grained and detailed (for algorithmic consumption) and an important but often missed part of data collection is capturing context (technical, business and otherwise). For instance, why was a certain action or decision appropriate given the context?
Be sure to capture data with machine consumption in mind rather than just human insights, and also capture as much of the context as possible.
5. Business context is also important.
Everyone focuses on the models, but just as important for AI success is how a business is structured around those models. Is there proper oversight? Are there workflows in place to take advantage of the insights gained from AI and halt any unintended outputs of models? Can you measure if your AI models are actually helping your business improve the customer experience or the bottom line?
At the Institute for Experiential AI, we advocate for creating organizations with an internal, proactive management team or tapping into experts who can help business leaders on demand. In operational settings, proving viability, sustainability and ROI is just as critical as avoiding risks.
6. Don’t forget about predictive AI.
While generative AI and LLMs have captured attention, the reality is that not all problems can be addressed by GenAI. Many problems are best addressed with predictive AI, which constitutes the majority of working AI applications out there and has been worked on for the past four decades.
Predictive AI can often produce faster, more stable and more reliable solutions much more economically. While GenAI will help us address many tasks in accelerating knowledge economy tasks, predictive AI continues to have a huge role to play.
7. Using AI responsibly brings real business value.
I am more convinced than ever that proper and responsible use of AI tools can bring real business value. Companies are now using AI to automate tedious tasks, supercharge efficiency, and improve the accuracy and effectiveness of several products and processes.
In this rapidly evolving economic landscape, I believe that companies that successfully and responsibly harness AI's capabilities, while also acknowledging and addressing its limitations, are poised to outpace those that remain hesitant to adopt these technologies.

title: Council Post: Unleashing A Strategic Sales System: How To Transform Your Business
text:
Thomas is the CEO of Instantly Relevant, where customers can grow their business with social media and technology.
In the ever-evolving digital landscape, businesses are increasingly turning to social media and artificial intelligence (AI) to boost their growth. However, without a systematic approach, these powerful tools can lead to guesswork, inefficiency and mediocre results. Let's explore how a well-structured sales system, exemplified by platforms like LinkedIn, can revolutionize your business trajectory.
The Chaos Before: A Tale Of Guesswork And Mediocrity
Once upon a time, in the not-so-distant past, businesses ventured into the digital realm armed with nothing but hope and a handful of random strategies. Marketing efforts on social media were often haphazard, characterized by a scattershot approach that targeted everyone and, paradoxically, no one. This lack of focus led to inefficiencies, wasted resources and a sea of "meh" outcomes. Imagine shooting arrows in the dark, hoping to hit a bullseye that you can't even see!
The Transformation: A Sales System That Works
Enter the era of strategic growth, where your business can thrive by adopting a phased sales system, integrating goals and AI-driven insights. This approach begins with defining clear objectives and unfolds through three critical phases: core, connect and convert.
1. Core: Establishing Foundations
Everything starts with clarity. What are your business goals? Who is your ideal customer? This phase is about establishing a rock-solid foundation for your sales strategy. It involves using AI to analyze data and identify your "profile-of-one"—that perfect customer whose needs align precisely with what you offer.
2. Connect: Building Relationships
Once your foundations are set, it's time to engage. This phase is all about connecting with your audience in a meaningful, altruistic way. Your social media presence, especially on platforms like LinkedIn, should reflect a genuine desire to add value to your audience. This involves sharing insightful content, participating in relevant conversations and using AI to understand and respond to emerging trends and customer preferences.
3. Convert: Sealing The Deal
Now, for the grand finale—conversion. This phase leverages your differentiated solutions and modern offer theory to convert connections into customers. It's about presenting your products or services in a way that resonates with your audience's specific needs, using AI to fine-tune your messaging and offers.
Key Tenets Of A Social Media Sales System
Any modern social media sales system should include the following:
1. Niche Focus: Target a specific audience. A well-defined niche can be the difference between shouting into the void and speaking directly into the ears of those who matter most.
2. Altruism In Engagement: Your interactions should be rooted in a genuine desire to help. This approach builds trust and establishes you as an authority in your field.
3. Differentiated Solutions: Stand out from the crowd. Offer something unique that addresses the specific pain points of your audience.
4. Leveraging AI And Modern Offer Theory: Use AI to gain insights into customer behavior and preferences, and craft offers that are almost impossible to refuse.
Navigating Pitfalls: Steering Clear Of Common Missteps
While implementing a strategic sales system is a game changer, there are pitfalls that businesses must conscientiously avoid to ensure sustainable success. Let's delve into some of these traps and understand how to steer clear.
1. Ego-Centric Approach: Remember, it's not about you; it's about your customers. An ego-centric strategy that focuses more on self-promotion rather than addressing customer needs is a surefire way to disengage your audience. Always keep the spotlight on how you can solve problems and add value to your customers' lives.
2. Overly Salesy Tactics: While the end goal is to convert prospects into customers, overtly sales-oriented tactics can be off-putting. The key is subtlety and value addition. Focus on nurturing relationships and building trust rather than pushing for a sale at every opportunity.
3. Misusing AI: AI is a powerful tool, but it's not a panacea. Relying on AI as a complete replacement for human insight and intuition can lead to a disconnect with your audience. Use AI as an accelerator to enhance your understanding of customer needs and market trends, not as a standalone solution.
4. Prioritizing Growth Over Service: While growth is essential, it should not come at the expense of deeply serving your customers. A business model prioritizes rapid growth over the quality of customer service can lead to short-term gains but long-term losses. Focus on deeply serving your customers, understanding their needs, and exceeding their expectations. This approach not only fosters loyalty but also transforms customers into enthusiastic promoters of your business.
By avoiding these pitfalls and maintaining a customer-centric, empathetic approach that leverages AI as an enabler rather than a crutch, businesses can build a sales system that not only drives growth but also fosters lasting customer relationships and brand loyalty.
The Afterglow: Results That Speak Volumes
With this systematic approach, the transformation is palpable. Businesses move from a state of uncertainty to a world where every action is purposeful and results-driven. Engagement rates soar, conversion rates climb and the overall return on investment (ROI) from social media activities skyrockets.
The Cherry On Top: A Referral System
No sales system is complete without a robust referral mechanism. Encourage satisfied customers to leave reviews on platforms like Google and Clutch—and to share their experiences through video, audio and text testimonials. This not only adds credibility to your brand but also harnesses the power of word-of-mouth in the digital age.
Conclusion: The Path Forward
The transition from a haphazard approach to a strategic sales system can be the turning point for businesses looking to harness the power of social media and AI. By setting clear goals, focusing on a niche audience, engaging altruistically, offering differentiated solutions and building a strong referral system, businesses can achieve remarkable growth and sustainability.
The future belongs to those who are ready to embrace this change and make the most of the digital opportunities that lie ahead. So, gear up, set your sights on your goals and let the magic of a structured sales system lead the way to unprecedented success!

title: Council Post: Empowering SMBs With Essential AI Technologies
text:

AI empowers SMBs to save time and money by automating repetitive tasks, freeing up valuable time for overworked employees to focus on higher-value activities. Case in point: In a separate survey, out of all the SMBs that implemented AI, 91% have seen an increase in success.
If SMBs wish to not only survive but thrive in the AI era, it’s crucial they gain access to digital tools that make use of the latest advancements in the technology, just like the bigger organizations do.
Based on our experience of offering an AI solution to the SMB market, here are the applications of AI technology that have proven to be most impactful for small businesses:
Strategic Planning
An AI-informed business strategy can empower SMBs to make better decisions with more foresight—a key component of staying competitive in an ever-evolving business landscape.
AI can rapidly analyze large volumes of data from various sources and identify patterns, trends and correlations that might not be apparent to the human eye. These insights aid in understanding market dynamics, customer behaviors, and competitive landscapes, all crucial for strategic decision-making. Similarly, these tools can continuously monitor competitors' activities, market trends and consumer preferences.
By compiling and analyzing this data, AI systems can offer decision support and recommend optimal courses of action for SMB leaders. Even the top-rated business consultant wouldn’t have the 360 view of an SMB’s performance the same way AI does and wouldn't be able to provide advice based on millions of data points.
Finances
AI tools designed for financial management are a boon for expense management and cost optimization. They can convert photos of receipts and PDF invoices into digital data, saving time on manually entering information. Additionally, they can automate and, in turn, expedite routine bookkeeping and accounting tasks such as data entry, invoice processing and expense categorization, which reduces human error.
With the ability to analyze spending patterns, AI tools can also inform decisions that improve cost efficiency, help negotiate better deals with suppliers and optimize inventory management to improve cash flow. AI algorithms that parse historical financial data and market trends can, therefore, help SMBs generate accurate forecasts and inform smart decisions regarding budgeting, investments and potential growth opportunities.
Marketing
Small-business owners are multitasker extraordinaires—they must juggle order fulfillment, inventory management and more, all while overseeing employees. Amid these pressing responsibilities, marketing often falls by the wayside.
Consider the 39% of SMBs who say marketing is their greatest challenge and the 60% who say their biggest challenge is attracting new customers. Here, AI is a two-in-one solution: It can help SMBs write marketing copy that strikes the right tone for their intended audience, saving them time and money and attracting new customers in the process.
AI tools can also automate lead generation by identifying potential leads and qualifying them based on predefined criteria. This helps in focusing efforts on recruiting leads who are more likely to become paying customers, optimizing both sales and marketing resources.
Customer Service
For SMBs—where every customer truly counts—good customer service is vital. But like marketing, customer service is yet another of the many balls that small-business owners are stretched thin to keep in the air. By integrating AI into customer service strategies, SMBs can improve customer experiences and target their audiences more effectively without unnecessarily sapping the time needed for their myriad other responsibilities.
AI chatbots offer instant and constant support for routine queries on products or services. And while AI is perfectly suited to smaller, standard support needs, it can always move more complex issues to human agents when necessary.
Big Gains For SMBs
AI stands as a transformative force for SMBs, unlocking their potential in various realms. While AI can be a game changer, its implementation needs to be tailored and carefully planned.
For AI to deliver real value, the insights it offers must go beyond generic advice that can be easily found through other sources. To produce personalized insights and advice, AI needs to access a considerable amount of data on each business. Without knowledge of the businesses offered services, target audience and pricing, how could AI possibly generate strategic or financial recommendations? Furthermore, AI’s ability to craft personalized marketing assets or skillfully respond to clients will be extremely limited without knowledge of the business.
The possibility of SMBs investing in data entry on this scale is unlikely. It would create administrative overhead, which is exactly what AI strives to eliminate. This is where SMB tech providers must rise to the challenge and introduce AI applications that already hold all the data needed.
AI has the power to work wonders for all small-business owners, giving them more time and funds to focus on what they set out to do in the first place—bring their business to the world. SMB tech providers are in a unique position to deliver the promise of AI to the SMB playground, bringing one of the most buzzing tech trends to those who need it most.

title: Council Post: What Every Leadership Team Needs To Know About Generative AI
text:
Andrew Duncan, CEO and Managing Partner, Infosys Consulting.
Generative AI is at a tipping point in technology adoption. It’s predicted to become a $1.3 trillion market by 2032, and it’s set to transform how we work and how companies generate revenue.
No firm can afford to ignore it. More than 20% of the over 400 CEOs surveyed by Gartner researchers in 2022 named AI as the technology with the most strategic value going forward. Additionally, a recent Infosys Knowledge Institute survey found that over 80% of employees believe that AI increases their productivity.
But when it comes to business applications, generative AI is still in its infancy, and executive leadership teams are understandably faced with a mountain of questions. Those I've spoken to are caught between embracing innovation and playing it safe.
Three Questions To Ask About Generative AI
The fact remains that most leaders want to know when to act—and how. Here are three questions executive leadership teams should ask before embracing generative AI.
1. How will generative AI impact my industry?
Generative AI is more than just a chatbot—it can amplify and automate workflows. Text generators like ChatGPT can already create marketing copy and personalized advertising that mirrors a brand’s tone of voice. Software developers can create entire lines of code, and manufacturers are accelerating design processes to realize ideas that can win greater market share.
But it’s easy to fall into the trap of plugging generative AI into existing workflows in isolated use cases that have little impact on the broader organization. Effective AI-first organizations, however, identify processes that can be enhanced with AI and build a comprehensive business case that strengthens adoption. Many successful use cases will be embedded in existing workflows, streamlining repetitive tasks to free up time for higher-value strategic activities.
Leadership teams should start by developing a business case centered around value capture and productivity improvements. They should actively identify internal, employee-driven use cases to uncover how generative AI can amplify their work. They should also take the time to see where adjustments and tweaks might be needed before taking use cases to external workflows. Adopting a fail-fast, learn-fast mindset will create space for innovation and learning. After all, leading an AI-centered organization means making assumptions, testing and experimentation.
2. What capabilities do we need to build?
Having the right skills and capabilities is vital to long-term success. Leadership teams should focus on building technical capabilities and upskilling their workforce to reflect the new skills needed in the AI-driven future.
Generative AI can supercharge the performance of programmers, designers, researchers, planners and marketers, to name a few. It can evolve how some jobs are done and see the emergence of entirely new roles to meet skills gaps.
Prompt engineering, for example, will become foundational in the AI-first organization. Infosys Knowledge Institute found that organizations like Google are investing millions in hiring prompt engineers to discover, test and document best practices for collaborating with AI. Technical capabilities and familiarity with the architecture and operation of large language models will become prized skills and are essential to developing AI capabilities.
As well as hiring new talent, executive leadership teams should focus on learning and development, equipping their people with the skills needed for the future of work. Offering training programs and hands-on skills development are essential to instilling AI in your organization’s culture while upskilling your teams so everyone can embrace and shape the path ahead. Leaders should foster a culture of continuous development in which employees are encouraged to innovate and experiment with AI tools.
3. How do we transform our operating model?
Generative AI has the potential to upend how organizations create new revenue streams and reset competitive balance across their industries. But more important than the introduction of the technology is how organizations are set up to take advantage of it.
Going AI-first means building talent, processes and systems to design and deliver AI services. Infosys' research defines four building blocks for the AI-first company: experience, engineering excellence, responsible design and a robust operating model. Leadership teams must rethink the customer and employee experience, reimagining everything from internal processes and workflows to customer journeys. Leaders will need to embed next-generation software development and platform engineering at the heart of their organizations, install robust processes to ensure that risks are mitigated and managed and develop the skills and talent required to enable faster time to value.
Remember: Action, Not Just Words
Ultimately, the question of how and when to adopt generative AI will vary from organization to organization. Technology adoption is moving at a lightning pace, and the gap between leaders and laggards is growing. The time for leadership teams to act is now.

title: Council Post: Why Product Management Will Be A Major Driver In Where AI Goes From Here
text:
SVP, Product Management: AI & ML, Developer Platforms, Core Banking Platform and Innovation Lab at Capital One.
When you think about the key drivers of a company’s innovation journey, product managers might not be the first to come to mind—but with the emergence of state-of-the-art AI, they should be.
As a longtime product leader at Capital One, I’ve seen firsthand how product managers can be the catalysts for innovation—even meaningful technical innovation. Many years ago while attending the NeurIPS conference, I was struck by how many data scientists come up with meaningful innovations that never actually impact real decisions and customer experiences.
As a product manager, I see it as my and my team's role to make sure that never happens. We should always be looking for applications with the latest and greatest technical capabilities and figuring out how to make a real-world impact with those advancements.
At Capital One, we have been successful at doing this in many ways over the years. For example, we have taken advantage of new advances in machine learning techniques to stop fraudsters; used big data to personalize the experiences of our customers; and are always looking out for our customers by using anomaly detection to flag things like the end of a free trial when we see a recurring charge increase significantly.
As companies race to unlock new AI capabilities, the role of product management becomes increasingly crucial. It plays a pivotal role in not only leveraging AI to enhance customer experiences but also in carefully assessing risks and making hard decisions to ensure human involvement in the decision-making process.
How can product leaders navigate the rapidly evolving AI landscape to meet their customers’ needs, deliver the most value and responsibly do it all with a network of disparate partners across the company? Here are a few best practices to help product leaders stay ahead of the curve as they consider AI in their world in 2024.
Avoid shiny-object syndrome.
Tech and product people love to build things. So it’s no surprise they sometimes get shiny-object syndrome, in which they lose sight of big-picture goals and start building products with hot new technology because, well, it’s exciting and new. One of the worst outcomes is to build something really cool—say a new machine learning mode—that no one uses because it doesn’t meet their needs or never gets integrated into downstream decisioning systems.
Product managers can play a key role in preventing shiny-object syndrome by understanding where to place the big bets on building new capabilities and experiences that can deliver unique, differentiated value, versus buying an off-the-shelf solution that would save time and resources and achieve the same result.
Understand where the leverage is and ruthlessly prioritize.
The main role of the product manager is to prioritize work to achieve the best outcome for the customer, whether that customer is within the company or outside it. In a space like AI, which has so many applications and tools, it’s impossible to prioritize everything. Taking a customer-backed approach helps product managers understand the real value of the capabilities they’re setting out to build in order to unlock as much of that value as soon as possible.
With long-term value in mind, the best product managers also do a lot of thinking about building tools and capabilities that can be extensible to other parts of the organization, because they meet the needs of many stakeholders. Reuse and standardization are some of the most underrated innovations.
Keep learning and building new skills.
To me, a good product manager is a good product manager. If you have the right mindset and take a customer-backed approach with a clear destination in mind, everything else (mostly) falls into place. But if you’re a product manager in a technical space that is working with AI capabilities—and soon, won’t that be all of us?—it’s important to stay sharp on the latest technical skills in the craft.
My company recently launched a product management machine learning certification program to equip our product managers with the skills they need to build advanced AI and machine learning capabilities into our products that will ultimately better serve our customers.
The best training and upskilling programs shouldn’t just teach product managers new technical skills. They should also help them find new ways to use these skills to communicate and collaborate with data scientists, engineers, designers and other partners—and identify opportunities where AI can make a real difference for customers.
New AI advances and capabilities are emerging nearly every day, and everyone is continuously learning and experimenting. One thing we can all agree on is that we don’t know what the world will look like in the future. I see incredible opportunities for product leaders to help our companies and customers understand the bigger picture of using AI to make everyone’s lives easier. It’s a fun space and an exciting time to be a part of this next wave of the technology revolution.

title: “Education Meets AI” At The 2024 World Economic Forum In Davos
text:
Government officials from Slovenia and the United Arab Emirates joined the leaders of two tech companies for a panel discussion on “Education Meets AI: Artificial Intelligence as Driving Force for the Economy and Society” at the 2024 World Economic Forum. Along with “novel opportunities for deeply personalized learning and tutoring,” participants discussed “uncharted risks for today’s learners in schools, universities and workplaces.”
Moderator Nzinga Qunta, anchor at the South African Broadcasting Corp., summarized three important issues that arose during the panel. AI learning extends beyond the classroom and is not defined by age or even physical space; we must remain vigilant to eliminate bias in the gathering of data; and perhaps most importantly, critical thinking is essential in evaluating AI.
Topics stressed by the panelists included AI tutoring, how and what we teach and the general importance of critical thinking.
AI Tutoring
All four panelists were enthusiastic about the use of AI to provide personalized, scalable tutoring outside the traditional classroom. Ahmad bin Abdullah Humaid Belhoul Al Falasi, Minister of Education of the United Arab Emirates, claimed, “Technology makes education scalable.” He explained that classes in the UAE are not affected, but “democratic tutoring,” available to all and based on the UAE curriculum, supplements classroom teaching.
The success of private tutoring is well documented, said Al Falasi, but not everyone can afford it. AI costs only a fraction of a human teacher and “It leaves the hardest part—the soft skills—to teachers.” Restricting AI to tutoring outside class also circumvents any suspicion teachers might have that they are being replaced.
AI Itself Is Not Stealing Jobs
A risk mentioned periodically is people’s resistance to AI based on the fear that humans might be replaced by computers. People must be informed that their jobs will not be taken by AI, but by people who know how to use AI. This might prove to be both an assurance to teachers and an incentive to learners.
How And What We Teach
“The promise of AI is personalized learning,” said Hadi Partovi, Founder and CEO of Code.org. His company is working with researchers at Stanford, to incorporate the latest thinking in pedagogy.
Al Falasi spoke from his experience tutoring his twin children, who have very different learning styles.
An example of how lessons are personalized to the learner’s interests was given in the discussion by an audience member. If the AI learned that a student was interested in soccer, the examples in the lessons provided by his company’s service might be drawn from soccer.
Even more intriguingly, this audience member pointed out that panelists had been assuming that AI is reliant on computer devices and the internet. His organization feeds information to learners via text messaging. Although there was no time to discuss this alternative, it suggested a way out of current bottlenecks in information delivery.
Panelists also concurred that not only how we teach, but what we teach needs to change. Emilija Stojmenova Duh, Minister of Digital Transformation of Slovenia, pointed out that in Slovenia, only “half the population has digital skills,” which are needed “not only for jobs, but for everyday life.” Women are not well represented in the sector, she said, and we must train “not only young people, but those who have completed school,” including retired people. If the general population does not have basic digital skills, they cannot make use of AI.
Jeffrey R. Tarr, CEO of Skillsoft, stressed the importance of workforce learning. “Generative AI opens new skills gaps when we haven’t even solved the first ones,” said Tarr. AI will be “the new front door to learning,” he claimed. “Coaching is a way we grow at the senior level,” noted Tarr, who sees AI as a way of extending coaching to everyone.
More STEM education would better equip people to understand and make use of AI. Here an interesting point was made about countries that might be considered to be at a disadvantage in adapting AI. Young countries have an advantage, according to Partovi, because they do not need to revise curricula that are 200 years old.
The Need For Critical Thinking
A Swiss attendee underlined the risk of mis- and disinformation, which might be amplified by AI. Duh and Partovi agreed heartily on the need for critical thinking.
Al Falasi gave an example of how critical thinking is taught along with AI in the UAE. Students are assigned to use ChatGPT. Then in class, they are asked to critically challenge the responses they got using ChatGPT.
The risks of mis- and disinformation go far beyond the use of AI in education. However, AI makes this risk so hazardous that the threat might turn into an opportunity. In acquiring AI skills, learners might find themselves mastering the even more valuable skill of critical thinking.

title: SAP BrandVoice: Learn How AI Expands Life Sciences Growth Potential
text:
By Aparna Seksaria, Global Practice Lead R&D Solutions – Life Sciences, SAP
The keys to leaving behind the competition and promoting organizational growth are changing significantly in the pharmaceutical industry – even to the extent where data and technology investments are emerging as pivotal factors in differentiation. Among midsize life sciences companies surveyed by IDC, 51% cited enabling digital transformation initiatives as their top business objective.
From attracting the attention of larger pharmaceutical enterprises for acquisitions to providing superior customer experiences and increasing customer loyalty, these companies have recognized the inherent value of having a robust IT infrastructure.
They’re not only unearthing new growth opportunities and enhancing services and product personalization, but also fortifying their supply chains and carving a path toward ongoing success in an increasingly diverse and competitive landscape.
Now, artificial intelligence (AI) presents new opportunities to advance into the next phase of their digital transformation journey. However, this latest development is more than just adopting recent technology or improving current practices. It’s forging a future where new ideas and higher success rates lead to a better understanding of innovative personalized medications and quicker, smoother launches of new life-saving therapies.
Adding a new cornerstone to the value paradigm
Midsize life sciences businesses wield a distinct advantage in their ability to adapt quickly, pivot deeply, and implement operational changes swiftly, compared to their larger competitors. Integrating AI into their processes, workflows, and business systems can enable more-efficient operations that yield faster and more-strategic outcomes.
For example, the synergy between AI adoption and the life sciences value chain will help scale R&D and production capabilities with real-time impact on demand and supply changes. Over time, firms can streamline operations and enhance decision-making through data-driven insights – both are pivotal for a competitive edge in promoting growth and efficiency.
Discover how digitalizing processes, products, services, and business models can be crucial to the growth of your midsize life science business. Read the IDC info snapshot, “Midsize Life Sciences Businesses Look to Supercharge Growth
No matter how critical, such changes often emerge through incremental steps of AI adoption rather than a singular transformative leap. By concentrating on smaller components and measuring results in manageable pieces, firms can realize quick wins in critical areas including planning, transportation management, sourcing, and procurement and build on them to offer uniquely differentiating value.
Cheerland Biotechnology Investment Co. Ltd. is a prime illustration of how AI amplifies the value of growing life sciences businesses. The company tightly integrated its operations by adopting a cloud ERP solution that offers AI, machine learning, robotic process automation, and support for integrated finance, supply chain, manufacturing, and sales and distribution processes. This includes removing internal barriers, applying rigid data protection and security practices, and enabling data-driven decision-making through access to rich data and analytics.
All these changes enabled Cheerland Biotechnology to achieve critical improvements, including 30% higher supply chain efficiency and 50% fewer current good manufacturing practices (cGMP) tickets.
Refocusing traditional ROI metrics toward value centricity
The full realization of AI’s potential relies on developing and adopting ROI metrics for digital investments that are unique to the business’s ecosystem. By steering away from traditional quantitative metrics such as cost reduction, product capacity, time to market, and revenue margins, businesses can deepen their understanding of value creation over a much longer time horizon.
This value-based mindset is particularly critical because AI impacts diverse business areas with smaller, tangible outcomes rippling throughout the business. These outcomes require nuanced evaluation that breaks down each contribution into measurable components – such as improving productivity, enhancing customer experience, and refining operational efficiency.
Interestingly, the case for value-based analysis isn’t entirely novel. It resonates deeply with existing industry methodologies for R&D, clinical trials, and other research-related activities managed with complex operational frameworks, stringent regulatory governance, and diverse ecosystem dependencies.
By applying this value-based approach to AI investments, companies can further transform their operations. They can better understand how to drive efficiency, speed, precision, and advantages where every moment and investment counts – especially in supply chain planning, scheduling, production processes, vendor selection, and delivering patient care.
Redefining an industry with real-time intelligence
As midsize life sciences companies continue to harness AI's transformative potential, a nuanced focus on tangible outcomes amplifies their role in reshaping the industry's competitive landscape. This evolution not only underscores the significance of technology but also heralds a future where AI-led innovations redefine the boundaries of possibility in advancing healthcare and scientific endeavors.

title: The 10 fastest-growing jobs in the U.S. right now—many can be remote and pay over $100,000
text:

Chief growth officer, sustainability analyst and artificial intelligence consultant are among the most in-demand roles companies are hiring for in the U.S., according to new research from LinkedIn.

Given LinkedIn's ranking is based on five years of data, it's clear that these are opportunities where companies have shown "consistent interest and commitment," says Andrew Seaman, senior managing editor for jobs and career development LinkedIn News. "These are sustainable careers, they're not just flashes in the pan," he adds.

Some companies are still reeling from the long, economic hangover of the Covid-19 pandemic and looking for ways to insulate themselves from future disruptions, says Seaman.

Sustainability jobs are also in high demand as more countries pledge to reduce carbon emissions and tighten environmental regulations.
"Even if you aren't interested in these specific jobs, paying attention to where demand is can help you navigate these rapid changes in the job market a little better and pivot accordingly," says Seaman. title: How this humanoid robot learned to make coffee by watching videos
text:
What if I told you that a robot can make you a cup of coffee just by watching a video of a human doing it?
It's almost hard to believe, but it actually happened.
Thanks to a breakthrough in artificial intelligence, humanoid robots can now watch and learn from humans, just like we do.
The company behind the coffee-making robot
The company behind this innovation is Figure, which has developed a full-body humanoid robot called Figure-01. This AI robot can walk, talk, and interact with its surroundings, and it can also learn new skills by watching videos.
MORE: THE NEXT GENERATION OF TESLA'S HUMANOID ROBOT MAKES IT DEBUT
How the robot was able to make a cup of coffee
Figure recently demonstrated how Figure-01 can make coffee using a Keurig machine. The demonstration took place at Figure’s headquarters in San Francisco, where a human asked Figure-01 to make him a coffee. The robot responded with a cheerful "Sure, I can do that!" and proceeded to the Keurig machine.
The robot had previously watched a video of a human making coffee using the same machine, and it had learned how to mimic the human’s actions. It used its vision system to recognize the machine and its parts, and its motion planning system to coordinate its movements.
It opened the hatch, inserted the pod, closed the hatch, and pressed the button, all by itself. It then waited for the coffee to be ready, and let the human grab the full cup out of the machine himself.
MORE: 10 COFFEE MAKERS TO MAKE YOUR MORNINGS BETTER
The whole process took less than a minute, and the robot did not need any human assistance or guidance. It was able to perform the task autonomously, using only the video as a reference. This is an example of end-to-end AI, where the neural networks take video in and trajectories out.
HOW AI ROBOT SMASHED HUMAN WORLD RECORD IN LABYRINTH, A CLASSIC MARBLE MAZE GAME
MORE: MEET THE WORLD'S FIRST AI MASSAGE ROBOT
What this means for AI and robotics
The demonstration was not only impressive but also significant and impactful. It showed that Figure-01 has added a new autonomous action to its library, which can be transferred to any other Figure robot running on the same system via swarm learning.
This means that if one robot learns something new, all the other robots can learn it, too, without having to watch the video themselves. This makes the learning process faster and more efficient and enables the robots to share their knowledge and skills with each other.
WHAT IS ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI)?
The demonstration also showed that this learning process could be used across a broad range of different tasks and that Figure-01 can learn to do anything from peeling bananas to using power tools to making art, all by watching videos. The robot can also learn not only what to do but also why and how to do it and how to adapt to different situations and contexts.
MORE: HOW THIS ROBOT HELPS YOU PROTECT AND CONNECT YOUR HOME
What’s next for Figure-01 and video learning?
The demonstration was just the beginning. Figure says that 01 can learn to do anything by watching videos and that it is constantly improving its capabilities and performance. The company has big plans for the future, and it wants to make its robot more versatile, creative, and collaborative.
Kurt's key takeaways
Imagine if Figure-01 could soon go find a cup in the kitchen, check that the Keurig’s plugged in and has plenty of water in it, make the press-button coffee, and bring it to your desk without spilling it, all by watching videos and using its walking and language capabilities. These are some of the possibilities and applications of video learning for robots, and they are not far from reality.

title: AMD And Nvidia Will Boil The Oceans
text:
There is a lot of gibbering about AI destroying humanity and it’s an obvious reflex. The first published work of fiction I ever had published at the tender age of 19, in 1982, was about AI and was pretty much along those lines. We’ve all grown up with HAL, the Forbin Project, the Terminator and a host of other such Frankenstein stories. However, a metal Arnie or a soft voiced HAL is not the risk.
The classic worry beyond extinction is redundancy: AI is going to put us all out of a job. But it is not.

The problem for us, was likely considered the problem for society then. Where are we going to get all that energy from? Because what is going to kick off is an explosion of energy consumption in a AI arms race with no natural ceiling.
